decay.note: Authored from botanical descriptions of bigleaf maple: five-lobed blades 15 to 30 cm across on petioles about as long, so 25 to 50 cm from the petiole's base to the tip, the largest leaves of any maple, yellow to gold in autumn and drying tan to brown, the large thin blades curling strongly as they dry, paler beneath; paired winged seeds, each wing 3 to 5 cm. The shape is the crown's own leaf. Colours and curl chosen by eye from photographs; numbers plausible, not measured.

look.note: Authored: the drawn look's mean hue at the brightness chosen by eye for this species' litter, the relief the drawing has, and a tile its pieces repeat on unseen. PlantGen's litter tests check the hue and relief against the drawing.
